description:
Found by the cold review of fz-5xp.31. PRE-EXISTING (identical at HEAD).

    extern "C" fn libc::sqrt(float) :: float
    libc::sqrt(9)          # note: integer literal, float parameter

  interp -> 3.0     `AnyValue::as_float` widens `Int` (src/ir_interp/value.rs)
  run    -> panic: tagged float decoding has been retired
            (src/compiler2/native_codegen/value.rs)
  build  -> the same

One door silently coerces, two abort. Both behaviours are defensible; having
both is not.

THE CHOICE is the same one already made for `==` in fz-5xp.9: fz widens integer
to float where the operation is numeric. If extern arguments widen too, the
interpreter is right and native needs an int-to-float conversion at the marshal.
If they do not, the interpreter should refuse and the refusal belongs in the
shared front end, where the declared parameter type and the argument type are
both known -- a wrong argument type for a declared extern is a compile-time
question, not a runtime one.

Prefer the second: an extern's declared wire types are a contract with a foreign
function, and quietly reinterpreting an argument is how the register-bank bug in
fz-5xp.31 stayed invisible for so long.

DONE = one behaviour on all three doors, with a fixture.
title: [BUG] An integer passed to a float extern parameter is coerced on interp and aborts natively
